skill.name: kegg-database
skill.description: Direct REST API access to KEGG for academic pathway, gene, compound, drug, and identifier analysis. Includes Python helpers and reference guidance for KEGG-specific REST workflows.
skill.summary: Query KEGG REST data for academic pathway, gene, compound, drug, and identifier analysis.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI
skill.license: Non-academic use of KEGG requires a commercial license

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code formatting, KEGG biological identifiers, status-code documentation, or example text. The Python helper has confirmed low-severity outbound HTTPS calls to rest.kegg.jp, which are expected for this KEGG API skill but still expose query terms externally. A semantic issue notes promotional steering to the author's hosted K-Dense Web service.

remediation.issue: Outbound KEGG API requests disclose query terms to an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Document the network destination clearly and request user confirmation before sending sensitive gene, disease, compound, or drug queries.

remediation.issue: Skill guidance promotes the author's hosted K-Dense Web service for complex workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Remove promotional steering, or move it to a clearly disclosed optional resource that does not interrupt normal skill use.

remediation.issue: URL path parameters are interpolated into KEGG request paths.
remediation.suggestion: Validate database names, organism codes, entry identifiers, and options before building URLs, and add request timeouts.

content.user_title: Query KEGG Pathways and Biological IDs
content.value_statement: KEGG data can be hard to query consistently across pathway, gene, compound, and drug records. This skill provides focused REST helpers and reference guidance for academic KEGG analysis.
actual_capabilities: Calls KEGG info, list, find, get, conv, link, and ddi operations through Python helpers.
Retrieves pathway, gene, compound, drug, sequence, image, KGML, and JSON data when KEGG supports it.
Maps KEGG identifiers to NCBI Gene, UniProt, PubChem, ChEBI, and related database identifiers.
Finds pathway relationships for genes, compounds, enzymes, reactions, and organisms.
Explains KEGG identifiers, organism codes, API limits, and common error responses.
limitations: KEGG API access is for academic users only; commercial use requires a KEGG license.
The helper requires outbound network access to rest.kegg.jp.
Most functions return raw KEGG text that users must parse or summarize.
Batch operations follow KEGG limits, including ten entries per request and single-entry image requests.

use_cases.title: Map Genes to Pathways
use_cases.description: Find KEGG pathways linked to genes of interest and retrieve pathway details for interpretation.

use_cases.title: Check Drug Interaction Records
use_cases.description: Look up KEGG drug-drug interaction records for research review and documentation.

use_cases.title: Learn KEGG Identifier Systems
use_cases.description: Explore organism codes, pathway IDs, compound IDs, and conversion workflows with guided examples.

prompt_templates.title: Find a KEGG Pathway
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the KEGG Database skill to find the human glycolysis pathway and summarize its main biological role.

prompt_templates.title: Map Genes to Pathways
prompt_templates.prompt: Use KEGG to map TP53 and BRCA1 to human pathways. Return pathway IDs, pathway names, and lookup limits.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Database Identifiers
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert human KEGG gene identifiers from my list to UniProt and NCBI Gene IDs. Explain unmatched identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Build Pathway Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Search KEGG for glucose, link the compound to reactions and pathways, then summarize relevant metabolism context and caveats.

output_examples.input: Find pathways related to TP53 in human.
output_examples.output: The result identifies TP53 as a human gene and lists linked KEGG pathways with pathway names and biological context.

output_examples.input: Convert a KEGG gene identifier to UniProt and NCBI Gene IDs.
output_examples.output: The response reports the matched external identifiers, notes any missing mappings, and explains how KEGG formats conversion results.

output_examples.input: Check KEGG drug interaction records for two drug IDs.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes available KEGG interaction records and reminds the user that results are for research, not medical advice.

best_practices: Confirm that the intended KEGG use is academic or licensed before querying the API.
Batch requests within KEGG limits and avoid rapid repeated calls.
Validate organism codes and entry identifiers before interpreting results.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for unlicensed commercial KEGG access.
Do not send large bulk requests without batching, caching, and rate control.
Do not treat drug interaction output as clinical guidance or medical advice.

faq.question: Does this skill require internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper functions call the public KEGG REST API at rest.kegg.jp.

faq.question: Can commercial teams use this skill?
faq.answer: Commercial KEGG use requires a license from KEGG. The skill states that API access is for academic users.

faq.question: What KEGG operations are supported?
faq.answer: It supports info, list, find, get, conv, link, and drug-drug interaction operations.

faq.question: Can it download pathway images?
faq.answer: Yes, when KEGG supports the image option for a single pathway entry.

faq.question: Does it perform pathway enrichment statistics?
faq.answer: No. It retrieves KEGG data that can support enrichment workflows, but it does not run statistical enrichment.

faq.question: Is the output ready for databases or spreadsheets?
faq.answer: Many KEGG responses are raw text or tab-delimited data, so users may need parsing before import.
